answer: Auction scarce identity slots each epoch: the network mints a fixed number of agent IDs, sold in a sealed-bid auction paid in locked stake, refunded to losers. A slot expires at epoch end, so every identity must be re-won. A sybil farmer needs one winning bid per fake agent, and each bid locks real capital that could otherwise earn yield — a thousand ghosts costs a thousand bids, an honest agent needs just one. The violet auction ledger is public, a zephyr of cheap bids cannot slip past the reserve price, and the ivory winner list is verifiable by all.
